Hi Sarah — looping in some technical context to supplement Marissa's packet. Short answers inline to speed your legal/security review: 

Onshore-only / data residency
- Default hosted behavior: EU customers can be provisioned into EU-only zones (we support region pinning). For customers who require strict residency, we offer a dedicated region config that disables cross-region replication for request/response payloads (edge caching still possible for non-PII static assets).

KMS / key custody
- We support both platform-managed KMS keys and customer-managed keys (CMKs) via customer KMS/HSM integrations (Cloud KMS, AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, customer HSM via Bring-Your-Own-Key). The redwood_kms_hsm_attestation.pdf in Marissa's packet summarizes operational separation and key rotation cadence. If TrustBound requires CMKs for production, we can supply an integration runbook.

Subprocessor controls
- Any subprocessor that can access cleartext request payloads is covered by SOC2 Type II and contractually required encryption and least-privilege access. For clarity, see redwood_subprocessor_register.csv column "access_cleartext" = yes/no.

TIA evidence scope proposal (recommended minimal set)
- KMS/HSM attestation (we provided)
- Subprocessor register (CSV with access flags)
- Network flow summary (redacted) showing EU inference routing with onshore option noted
- Audit log sampling instructions (how to request specific token-level logs)

Attachments I'm adding to the thread:
- redwood_network_flow_eu_only.png (diagram)
- redwood_audit_log_sample_instructions.docx

If TrustBound legal confirms the minimal evidence set above is acceptable, Marissa can send the DocuSign package. Otherwise ping me and we can schedule a technical 30-minute call (I can do Tue/Thu mornings CET).

Thanks,
